history: From the Savoy Cocktail Book, 1930, attributed to the Hotel Europe in Amsterdam.
whyItWorks: Vermouth-forward and barely 18% ABV, but the Bénédictine’s honey and the absinthe’s anise give it a length that most low-proof drinks lack.
steps: Stir vermouth, Bénédictine and absinthe with ice until well chilled.
Express an orange twist over the top and drop it in.
techniqueNotes: Use fresh vermouth. In a drink this vermouth-heavy, an open bottle that has been out a month is the whole flavor.
Three dashes of absinthe, not a rinse—it is a seasoning here.

recommendedBottles.rationale: Whatever is freshest; this drink hides nothing.

substitutions.notes: Chartreuse is drier and more herbal—cut to ½ oz.
Not the same, but keeps the drink balanced if absinthe is out.

name: Chrysanthemum
description: Dry vermouth and Bénédictine with an absinthe lift—a low-proof aperitif that eats like a much bigger drink.
